metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable entry point is present (frmCustomer.frm defines VB.Form frmCustomer with a Form_Load bootstrap and ADODB data access) and README.md describes a distributed Win32 desktop EXE. No second deployable unit (not monorepo), no library packaging manifest, and no resource-provisioning IaC or deployment-only config. Residual runnable-app case → application.
metadata.archetype_justification: No message-queue consumers and no multi-service orchestration. The system owns persistent state (ADODB connection to S:\CRM\sales.mdb) and performs entity writes (INSERT INTO Customers) rather than read-heavy querying — stateful-crud.
metadata.agent_scope_reasoning: has_write_operations = true (cmdSave_Click executes INSERT INTO Customers against the Access datastore), so agent_scope resolves to write-enabled per Step 1.5.

tech_stack.framework: VB6 forms + ADODB / Microsoft Jet OLEDB 4.0; Crystal Reports 8.5
tech_stack.architecture: Win32 desktop two-tier client-server: hand-distributed EXE reading/writing a Microsoft Access 2003 .mdb on an SMB file share, with a nightly DTS/SSIS sync to SQL Server 2012 for reporting

findings.title: Documented API Interface
findings.description: No programmatic interface of any kind exists. The only integration surface is the VB6 form `frmCustomer` in `frmCustomer.frm`, which opens an ADODB connection directly to a Microsoft Access file (`Provider=Microsoft.Jet.OLEDB.4.0;Data Source=S:\CRM\sales.mdb`, lines 19-21) and executes inline SQL from a button click handler (`cmdSave_Click`, lines 24-34). README.md documents the integration model as 'a Microsoft Access (.mdb) file on a shared network drive' with a nightly DTS/SSIS sync to SQL Server — i.e. file-based and database-level exchange. Searched for: REST route definitions, Spring/Flask/Express handlers, `.graphql`/`.gql`, `openapi.*`/`swagger.*`, AsyncAPI, `.smithy`, RPA/Selenium scripts — zero results across the 3 tracked files.
findings.gap: There is no REST, GraphQL, gRPC or AsyncAPI interface. Any agent integration would require direct Jet/OLEDB access to an .mdb file on an SMB share, or UI automation of a Win32 form — both brittle, unauditable, and unsupported for concurrent machine-speed callers.
findings.recommendation: Expose customer operations behind a service API before any agent integration. Target: migrate the Access data to a managed relational store (Amazon RDS/Aurora) and front it with a documented HTTP API (API Gateway + application service) that becomes the single agent-facing contract; retire direct .mdb access.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Define the customer-maintenance operations (create/read/update customer) as an HTTP API contract and stand up a service in front of the migrated datastore.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Agents call a versioned, documented HTTP API; no caller touches the .mdb file or the Access schema directly.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface exists (`has_http_rpc_surface = false`): `frmCustomer.frm` is a Win32 form with ADODB data access only. No `openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.smithy`, or AsyncAPI file is present in the repository.
findings.gap: No machine-readable specification — but there is no callable API surface for a spec to describe. Surface-flag calibration applies: 'No HTTP/RPC surface — machine-readable spec is not applicable.'
findings.recommendation: When the API from API-Q1 is introduced, generate an OpenAPI document from the implementation annotations and publish it as the agent tool-binding source.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No API responses exist to structure. Error handling in `frmCustomer.frm` is `On Error Resume Next` followed by a `MsgBox` dialog ('Could not save (record may be locked). Try again.', lines 28-33) — a human-facing modal with no error code, no category, and no retryable indicator. The error is then cleared (`Err.Clear`).
findings.gap: Failures are swallowed and surfaced only as UI text. Surface-flag calibration applies (no HTTP/RPC surface), so this is recorded as INFO rather than RISK-QUALITY.
findings.recommendation: Replace `On Error Resume Next` with explicit error propagation now, and define a structured error envelope (code, message, retryable) as part of the API introduced in API-Q1.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 24-34) performs an unconditional `INSERT INTO Customers (Name, CreatedBy, CreatedOn)` with no idempotency key, no business-key uniqueness check, and no read-before-write. Because errors are swallowed by `On Error Resume Next`, the caller cannot distinguish 'insert succeeded' from 'insert failed', and the user-facing message explicitly instructs 'Try again.' — a retry path that creates duplicate customer rows. No unique constraint is declared anywhere in the repository (no schema or migration files exist).
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism: retries duplicate records. Combined with swallowed errors, the retry instruction is built into the UI.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an idempotency key (or a natural-key unique constraint on Customers) and make the write path return a deterministic result for repeated identical requests before exposing writes to any retrying caller.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: agent_scope is 'write-enabled' (inferred from has_write_operations=true) — evaluated as BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The system's only operation is a non-idempotent INSERT with swallowed errors and a UI-level retry prompt; a retrying agent would duplicate customer records at machine speed.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add a unique constraint on the Customers business key and return an explicit success/failure result from the save path instead of `On Error Resume Next`.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Repeated identical write requests produce exactly one record and a deterministic response.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission exists. State changes are written directly to the Access database by `cn.Execute sql` (frmCustomer.frm line 29) with no notification path. README.md describes downstream propagation as 'a nightly sync job to a SQL Server reporting database' via a scheduled DTS/SSIS package — batch, once per day. No webhooks, SNS/EventBridge/SQS, Kafka, or CDC pipeline is present.
findings.gap: No event or webhook surface; the only change-propagation mechanism is a nightly batch sync, giving downstream consumers up to 24 hours of staleness.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are a target, emit domain events (e.g. EventBridge) from the service introduced in API-Q1 rather than relying on nightly batch sync.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: There is no authentication mechanism. The application connects to the data store with a single hardcoded Jet database password (`Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw"`, frmCustomer.frm line 8; used in the connection string at lines 19-21) shared by every copy of the EXE on every field laptop. Caller identity is taken from `Environ("USERNAME")` (line 27) — a client-side environment variable that is trivially spoofable and is not authenticated by the database. Searched for: OAuth2/client-credentials flows, API keys with principal attribution, mTLS config, service accounts, Cognito/IAM/API Gateway authorizers — none present.
findings.gap: No machine identity, no principal authentication, and no trustworthy principal attribution. Every caller is indistinguishable at the data layer, so no downstream authorization or audit decision can be relied upon.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an identity provider and machine-identity authentication (e.g. OAuth 2.0 client credentials or IAM-authenticated service access) in front of the migrated datastore, with per-agent principals and no shared database credential.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Remove the shared Jet database password from the client and route data access through an authenticated service identity instead of client-side `Environ("USERNAME")`.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Each caller — human or agent — authenticates as a distinct, revocable principal that the data layer can attribute.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: Authorization is binary and shared: possession of the Jet database password (`DB_PW`, frmCustomer.frm line 8) grants full Jet/OLEDB access to `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` (line 7). There is no role model, no per-caller permission set, and no mechanism to grant read-only access to a subset of tables or rows. No IAM policies, resource policies, or condition keys exist (no IaC in the repository).
findings.gap: All authorization is coarse-grained — a single shared credential conveys full database access, so an agent identity cannot be scoped down to read-only or to specific resources.
findings.recommendation: Define scoped roles at the service/datastore layer (read-only, customer-write) and bind agent principals to the narrowest role once AUTH-Q1 identity exists.

compensating_controls: Restrict the agent to an isolated read-only replica of the data rather than the shared .mdb credential.
Mediate all agent access through a human-operated service account with an explicit allowlist of operations.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 24-34) issues raw SQL over an ADODB connection opened with full database rights; the same credential can `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` any table in `sales.mdb`. Searched for `canRead`/`canWrite`/`canDelete`-style checks, ABAC/RBAC definitions, permission matrices and method-level authorization — none present.
findings.gap: The data layer cannot allow read without also allowing delete. An agent granted the ability to read customers inherently has the ability to destroy them.
findings.recommendation: Enforce action-level permissions in the service layer introduced in API-Q1 (separate read, create, update, delete grants per principal) and revoke direct SQL execution rights from callers.

compensating_controls: Grant the agent only SELECT rights on a dedicated database login until action-level checks exist.
Route all mutating operations through a human-approved batch process rather than the agent path.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation or delegation exists. The only identity signal is the client-side value of `Environ("USERNAME")` string-concatenated into the `CreatedBy` column (frmCustomer.frm line 27). There is no token, no JWT parsing, no on-behalf-of flow, and no way to distinguish a caller acting as itself from a caller acting on behalf of a specific user — the archetype is `stateful-crud`, so no INFO downgrade applies.
findings.gap: An agent acting on behalf of a user cannot be bounded by that user's permissions, and the `CreatedBy` attribution it writes is caller-asserted and unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Carry a verified identity (token-based, with distinct agent-as-self and agent-on-behalf-of-user modes) through the service layer and populate `CreatedBy` from the authenticated principal, never from a client-supplied environment variable.

compensating_controls: Restrict the agent to a single dedicated principal with its own narrow permissions and do not use it for on-behalf-of-user workflows.
Record the orchestration-layer user context in an external audit store that the agent cannot write to.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded in source and compiled into the distributed binary: `Private Const DB_PATH As String = "S:\CRM\sales.mdb"` and `Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw"` (frmCustomer.frm lines 7-8), interpolated into the connection string at lines 19-21. README.md independently records this as a known issue: 'ODBC connection string with credentials embedded in the EXE'. The password value indicates no rotation since 2005. No secrets manager, Vault client, or parameter-store reference exists; `.gitignore` excludes `.env` files but no secret-management mechanism replaces them.
findings.gap: A static, unrotated, shared credential is embedded in code and in every deployed EXE. Anything that can read the binary or the repository — including a prompt-injected agent with file access — obtains full database access.
findings.recommendation: Move the credential to a managed secret store (AWS Secrets Manager) with rotation, remove the constants from source, and rotate the existing password immediately since it is exposed in version control history.

compensating_controls: Rotate the Jet password and restrict NTFS/share permissions on S:\CRM so only the service principal can open the file.
Block agent file-system access to the repository and the distributed EXE so the constant cannot be read.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: There is no audit log. The single write path (`cn.Execute sql`, frmCustomer.frm line 29) records only a `CreatedBy` column populated from the client-controlled `Environ("USERNAME")` value (line 27) inside the same mutable Access file it is auditing. Errors are discarded by `On Error Resume Next` (line 28), so failed writes leave no trace at all. Searched for CloudTrail/CloudWatch configuration, log retention policy, object-lock log storage and any logging framework — none present (no IaC, no config files beyond `.gitignore`).
findings.gap: No immutable, tamper-evident record of write operations and no verifiable principal attribution. Agent-initiated writes could not be reconstructed, attributed, or proven for compliance or forensics.
findings.recommendation: Emit an append-only audit record (authenticated principal, operation, timestamp, outcome) to tamper-evident storage outside the application's own writable datastore before enabling any write-capable agent.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: agent_scope is 'write-enabled' (inferred from has_write_operations=true) — evaluated as BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The system performs state-mutating writes with no immutable audit trail and only spoofable, self-asserted attribution stored in the same mutable .mdb file, so write-enabled agent actions would be undetectable and unprovable.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Stop swallowing errors and write an append-only audit entry for every save attempt to storage the application cannot rewrite.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every write carries an immutable, tamper-evident audit record naming the authenticated principal and outcome.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: There is no revocable identity to suspend. Access is conveyed by the shared compiled-in password (`DB_PW`, frmCustomer.frm line 8); revoking it requires changing the Jet database password and recompiling and hand-redistributing the EXE to every laptop — README.md states 'Distribution: EXE copied to each laptop by hand' and 'No installer; deployment is "copy the EXE and the .mdb template"'. No API key revocation, role deactivation, or account-disable mechanism exists.
findings.gap: A misbehaving caller cannot be isolated without revoking access for every user of the application simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Issue per-principal credentials through the identity provider from AUTH-Q1 so a single agent identity can be disabled immediately without affecting other callers.

compensating_controls: Place the agent behind a proxy/service account whose credentials can be revoked independently of the shared EXE password.
Operate the agent only during supervised windows with a documented manual kill switch (disable the share ACL for the agent principal).

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: No transaction, compensation, or rollback support exists. `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 24-34) executes a bare `cn.Execute sql` with no `BeginTrans`/`CommitTrans`/`RollbackTrans`, no saga or compensating action, and no undo path. `On Error Resume Next` (line 28) actively discards the failure signal, and `Form_Unload` closes the connection the same way (lines 36-40). README.md records that the Access file 'corrupts under concurrent writes (~monthly)' — partial-write damage is an observed operational reality, not a hypothetical.
findings.gap: A multi-step or failed write leaves the database in a partial state with no rollback and no recorded failure. There is no mechanism to undo an agent-initiated write.
findings.recommendation: Wrap write sequences in explicit transactions with error propagation (and provide an explicit reversal operation for each exposed write) before allowing any autonomous write caller.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: agent_scope is 'write-enabled' (inferred from has_write_operations=true) — evaluated as BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Writes are non-transactional and failures are silently swallowed, so a failed agent write sequence cannot be detected or compensated; the README documents recurring data corruption from exactly this pattern.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Remove `On Error Resume Next` from the write path and wrap `cn.Execute` in an explicit ADODB transaction with rollback on error.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every write is atomic, failures are surfaced to the caller, and each exposed write has a documented compensating operation.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: No queryable state interface exists. `frmCustomer.frm` contains exactly one data operation — an `INSERT` in `cmdSave_Click` (lines 24-34). There is no SELECT, no read-before-write, no status field, and no GET-equivalent surface; the form's only control bound to data is the `txtName` text box. State can only be inspected by opening the .mdb file directly.
findings.gap: A caller cannot inspect existing customer state before acting, so it cannot tell whether a record already exists — which compounds the idempotency gap in API-Q4.
findings.recommendation: Expose read operations (get/list customer) alongside the write path so callers can verify current state before mutating it.

compensating_controls: Provide the agent a read-only query path over the nightly SQL Server reporting copy for state inspection.
Require the orchestration layer to supply existing-record context rather than letting the agent assume state.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency control exists. The write is a fire-and-forget `cn.Execute` against a Jet/OLEDB file on an SMB share (frmCustomer.frm lines 19-21, 29) with no version field, no `If-Match`/ETag equivalent, no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, and no conflict-resolution logic. The only concurrency handling is a `MsgBox` telling the user 'record may be locked... Try again.' (line 31). README.md confirms the consequences: 'Access .mdb on a file share corrupts under concurrent writes (~monthly)' and 'No real multi-user locking; "record locked" errors are common'.
findings.gap: Concurrent writers corrupt the data file — an already-observed monthly failure. Multiple concurrent agent instances would multiply write contention on a store with no locking discipline.
findings.recommendation: Migrate off file-share Jet to a server-based database with real transaction isolation, and add optimistic concurrency (row version) on customer records before allowing concurrent write callers.

compensating_controls: Serialize all agent writes through a single-threaded queue so only one write is in flight at a time.
Cap the agent to one concurrent instance and schedule it outside field-sales working hours.

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: The application depends on an external resource — the `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` file on an SMB share (frmCustomer.frm line 7, opened at lines 19-21) — with no resilience controls: no timeout on `cn.Open`, no retry or backoff, no circuit breaker, and no connection-failure handling (`Form_Load` has no error handler at all, lines 17-22). README.md notes the dependency is a single point of failure: 'File share is a single Windows file server with no failover'.
findings.gap: A slow or unavailable file share produces an unhandled failure or an indefinite hang, and repeated caller retries apply unbounded pressure to a dependency with no failover.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit connection timeouts and bounded retry with backoff around data access, and introduce a circuit breaker in the service layer from API-Q1 so dependency failure degrades predictably.

compensating_controls: Enforce caller-side timeouts and a retry budget in the agent orchestration layer.
Add a health probe on the share and halt agent invocation automatically when the probe fails.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: There is no API layer to throttle: `has_http_rpc_surface` is false — `frmCustomer.frm` is a Win32 form whose only data path is a direct ADODB connection (lines 19-21). No API Gateway configuration, WAF rate rule, or rate-limiting middleware exists (no IaC or config files in the repository). The effective limiter today is human click rate on `cmdSave`.
findings.gap: No rate limiting exists, but surface-flag calibration applies: 'System exposes no HTTP/RPC surface — API-layer rate limiting is not applicable.' Request-rate protection would have to be introduced along with the API itself.
findings.recommendation: Define throttling limits (per-principal request quotas) as part of the API introduced in API-Q1, since the underlying Jet data store cannot absorb machine-speed write traffic.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain limits exist. `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 24-34) imposes no cap on records created, no bulk-operation size limit, no per-caller quota, and no spend threshold; nothing in the repository is configurable at all (no config files beyond `.gitignore`). A caller invoking the write path in a loop would be bounded only by the Access file's own 2 GB limit and its tendency to corrupt.
findings.gap: There is no way to cap the blast radius of a caller executing correct-but-catastrophic logic — e.g. inserting thousands of customer rows into a file store that corrupts under write pressure.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-principal business transaction limits (max records created per run/hour, max bulk operation size) in the service layer from API-Q1, configurable independently of request-rate throttling.

compensating_controls: Enforce a hard per-run write budget in the agent orchestration layer and abort on exceedance.
Require human batch review for any run proposing more than a fixed small number of record changes.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: There is no draft or pending state. The `Customers` insert in `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) writes `Name`, `CreatedBy`, `CreatedOn` only — no status column, no state machine, and no two-step create-then-confirm pattern. The write is committed immediately on button click with no reviewable intermediate record.
findings.gap: Every write is immediately final, so a proposed change cannot be staged for human review before it becomes authoritative data.
findings.recommendation: Add a status field (e.g. `PENDING_REVIEW` / `ACTIVE`) and a confirm operation so agent-proposed records land in a reviewable state before becoming live.

compensating_controls: Have the agent write proposals to a separate staging table or file that a human promotes manually.
Keep the agent in propose-only mode: it generates the record payload, a human performs the save in the form.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval gate mechanism exists. `cmdSave_Click` executes the insert directly (frmCustomer.frm line 29) with no confirmation step, no approval endpoint, and no operation-level configuration flag — the application has no configuration surface at all. The only prompt in the code is a post-failure `MsgBox` (line 31), not a pre-execution approval.
findings.gap: High-risk operations cannot be configured to require human approval at the application layer, so there is no defense-in-depth beneath whatever gate the orchestration layer provides.
findings.recommendation: Make write operations approval-gated per operation type in the service layer from API-Q1 (request → approve → execute), so approval cannot be bypassed by calling the data layer directly.

compensating_controls: Place a human approval step in the agent orchestration layer before any invocation of the write path.
Restrict the agent's credential to read-only and require a human operator to perform all commits.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment exists. README.md states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine' and describes a single production data path — `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` on the shared drive — hardcoded as a constant with an explicit instruction not to change it: 'DO NOT change the .mdb path - field laptops are mapped to S:\' (frmCustomer.frm lines 5, 7). There are no environment-specific configurations, no seed data scripts, and no synthetic data generators in the repository.
findings.gap: Because the database path is a compile-time constant pointing at production, there is no way to exercise the write path against production-shaped data without touching live customer records.
findings.recommendation: Externalize the data source to configuration and stand up a staging copy of the database with representative data so caller behaviour can be validated before production.

compensating_controls: Create a copy of sales.mdb on a non-production share and build a separate test binary pointed at it for agent dry runs.
Validate all agent behaviour in read-only mode against the SQL Server reporting replica before enabling writes.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: `has_persistent_data_store` is true and the store holds customer business records — `frmCustomer.frm` writes a `Customers` table with `Name`, `CreatedBy`, `CreatedOn` (lines 25-27) into `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` (line 7), and README.md describes the system as a 'Sales CRM' whose Access file is the system of record for the field sales team. Customer names and the operator's Windows username are personal data. Stage B — B1: there is no response-scoping layer of any kind; the only integration path is full Jet/OLEDB access to the .mdb file (lines 19-21), which grants every column of every table to any caller holding `DB_PW`. No projections, DTOs, serializer exclusions, or field-level authorization exist. B2: no access-control differentiation — a single shared password is the whole authorization model (line 8). B3: no classification metadata — no tags, field annotations, data catalog, or PII tooling anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: Agent-facing access is unscoped at every layer: no field filtering (B1), no sensitive-vs-non-sensitive access differentiation (B2), and no classification metadata (B3). A caller granted access to create a customer necessarily has read access to the entire CRM dataset.
findings.recommendation: Front the data with a service that returns explicit field projections, split permissions by data domain, and classify the customer fields; no caller should hold direct .mdb credentials.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: agent_scope is 'write-enabled' (inferred from has_write_operations=true) — B1 fires as BLOCKER; overall DATA-Q1 = BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: B1 fired because there is no API response layer at all — integration is direct Jet/OLEDB access to sales.mdb with the shared database password, so every sensitive column is exposed to any agent-capable caller, and the scope is write-enabled.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Stop distributing the database credential to callers and introduce a mediated read path that returns only explicitly selected, non-sensitive fields.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Agent-facing responses are field-scoped projections, access is differentiated by data domain, and customer fields carry classification metadata.

b1.reasoning: No API response scoping exists; direct .mdb access with DB_PW exposes all columns of all tables (frmCustomer.frm lines 8, 19-21).

b2.reasoning: A single shared Jet password is the entire authorization model — no differentiation between sensitive and non-sensitive data access (frmCustomer.frm line 8).

b3.reasoning: No classification tags, field-level sensitivity annotations, data catalog, or PII detection tooling present in the repository.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The system holds persistent customer data (`has_persistent_data_store` = true) in `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` on an SMB share (frmCustomer.frm line 7) with a nightly copy into a SQL Server 2012 reporting database (README.md). No residency or sovereignty control or statement exists anywhere in the repository: searched README.md, `.gitignore`, and `frmCustomer.frm` for GDPR/LGPD/HIPAA references, region-specific storage configuration, cross-region replication settings, and data sovereignty policy — zero results. The physical location of the file server and the reporting database is undocumented, and there is no IaC to pin it.
findings.gap: The jurisdiction of the customer data is undetermined and unconstrained, and there is no technical control preventing data read from the .mdb from being transmitted to an out-of-region processor (including an LLM endpoint).
findings.recommendation: Determine and document the residency requirements for the CRM customer dataset, record the authoritative storage location, and pin processing (including any LLM endpoint) to a compliant region before any agent reads this data.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: agent_scope is 'write-enabled' (inferred from has_write_operations=true) — evaluated as BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The system persists customer personal data with no documented residency constraint and no region pinning, so an agent could move regulated data across a compliance boundary with no control detecting it.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Document the data classification and residency obligations for the CRM dataset and the physical location of the file server and reporting database.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Residency requirements are explicit, storage and processing regions are pinned in configuration, and cross-boundary transfer is technically blocked.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation. `cmdSave_Click` concatenates `txtName.Text` and `Environ("USERNAME")` directly into an SQL string (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) — the code's own comment states 'String-concatenated SQL - no parameters (injection risk)'. There is no length check, no type or format validation, no escaping, no parameterized command (`ADODB.Command` with parameters is not used), and no request-size limit. Validation failures cannot be reported because `On Error Resume Next` (line 28) discards all errors and the only feedback is a generic `MsgBox` with no field identification (line 31).
findings.gap: Malformed or adversarial input is accepted and executed as SQL. A caller cannot self-correct because rejections are neither structured nor, in most cases, reported at all. This is an exploitable SQL injection path, reachable by anything that can set the Name value.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized `ADODB.Command` parameters, add explicit field validation (length, allowed characters) and return structured, field-level rejection messages instead of swallowing errors.

compensating_controls: Validate and allowlist-sanitize the Name value in the caller/orchestration layer before invoking the write path.
Grant the write principal INSERT-only rights so an injected statement cannot drop or read other tables.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Temporal metadata is minimal and locally-scoped. The insert sets `CreatedOn` from VB6 `Now()` (frmCustomer.frm line 26), which returns the client laptop's local system time with no timezone normalization and no UTC storage — field laptops may differ in clock and timezone. There is no `updated_at`/`LastModified` column, no event-time field, and no freshness signal; README.md notes downstream reporting data is refreshed by a nightly batch, so consumers of the reporting copy can be up to 24 hours stale with no indicator.
findings.gap: Timestamps are unnormalized client local time and there is no update timestamp or staleness/consistency signal, so a caller cannot reliably reason about record age or whether data it reads is current.
findings.recommendation: Store timestamps in UTC from a single authoritative source, add a last-updated column, and expose a freshness indicator (e.g. last-sync time) on any read path offered to agents.

compensating_controls: Have the orchestration layer stamp its own UTC timestamps on records it submits and treat CreatedOn as advisory.
Expose the nightly sync completion time to the agent so it can bound the staleness of reporting-database reads.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: There is no redaction mechanism and no logging discipline. The system holds customer personal data (`has_persistent_data_store` = true, `Customers` table with `Name` and `CreatedBy`, frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) but has no structured logging, no log scrubbing middleware, no PII masking utility, and no CloudWatch/Macie filters — searched the full repository (3 tracked files) for any logging framework or masking pattern with zero results. The only error surface is a `MsgBox` dialog (line 31). `.gitignore` excludes `*.log`, which indicates log files are produced somewhere in the operational process but no content control governs them; the full SQL statement — including the customer name — is held in the `sql` variable and would appear verbatim in any debugger, crash dump, or future log statement.
findings.gap: No redaction control exists for a system that handles customer PII, so any future or operational logging (including crash dumps and the nightly sync job) carries unmasked personal data into observable surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Introduce structured logging with an explicit PII allowlist/masking layer before adding any diagnostic logging to this write path, and confirm the nightly DTS/SSIS sync does not log row contents.

compensating_controls: Prohibit the agent from echoing retrieved customer field values into its own transcripts or logs.
Restrict access to any produced .log files and crash dumps to the same control set as the customer database.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality measurement exists for the CRM dataset held in `S:\CRM\sales.mdb`. There are no profiling reports, null-rate or duplicate-detection checks, freshness SLAs, or quality dashboards in the repository. The known-issues list in README.md points the other way: monthly file corruption under concurrent writes and frequent 'record locked' errors, plus the absence of any uniqueness enforcement (API-Q4) which makes duplicate customer rows likely.
findings.gap: Dataset completeness and duplication rates are unmeasured, and documented corruption events make quality degradation likely rather than hypothetical.
findings.recommendation: Profile the Customers table (null rates, duplicate names, orphan rows) and establish a baseline quality metric before an agent reasons over this data.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: There are no versioned contracts of any kind. The `Customers` schema is implied only by the inline SQL statement in `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) and lives inside the binary .mdb file; there are no migration files, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf definitions, no schema registry, no `/v1/` style versioning, no changelog, and no breaking-change detection (there is no CI pipeline at all — README.md: 'No tests, no build server'). A schema change in the Access file would silently break every compiled client.
findings.gap: Schema and contract changes are undetectable and unversioned, so any caller binding to this data — including an agent tool definition — breaks silently when the .mdb schema changes.
findings.recommendation: Extract the schema into version-controlled migration files, publish a versioned contract for the data shape, and add breaking-change detection to a build pipeline.

compensating_controls: Pin the agent tool definition to a schema snapshot and re-validate it on a scheduled cadence.
Add a startup assertion that verifies expected columns exist before the agent path executes.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: The field names that do exist are semantically clear: `Customers (Name, CreatedBy, CreatedOn)` in the insert statement (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) are readable, unabbreviated, and need no data dictionary. VB6 control and constant naming follows a conventional Hungarian prefix style (`frmCustomer`, `cmdSave`, `txtName`, `cn`, `DB_PATH`) which is interpretable in context. No legacy coded field names (e.g. `CUST_TYP_CD`) appear in the visible schema; however only three columns are visible in source — the remainder of the Access schema is inside the binary .mdb and was not assessable.
findings.gap: The visible schema is agent-friendly. The unassessable remainder of the .mdb schema is the open question, not the naming convention.
findings.recommendation: Export the full Access schema to text and review the remaining column names for legacy abbreviations before building agent tool definitions.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists. The repository contains no data dictionary, schema documentation, catalog entries, or metadata files — README.md documents runtime architecture only, and the authoritative schema is embedded in the binary `sales.mdb` on the file share (frmCustomer.frm line 7). The nightly DTS/SSIS package that populates the SQL Server reporting database is also not in the repository, so the downstream mapping is undocumented here.
findings.gap: What the CRM dataset contains and what its fields mean is undiscoverable from the repository, so agent tool definitions would have to be reverse-engineered from the .mdb file.
findings.recommendation: Export the Access schema and register the dataset (and its nightly reporting projection) in a catalog or at minimum a checked-in data dictionary.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: There is no tracing and no logging. `frmCustomer.frm` contains no logging statements, no correlation or request identifier, no OpenTelemetry/X-Ray instrumentation, and no structured output of any kind; the three error handlers are `On Error Resume Next` (lines 28, 37) and a `MsgBox` (line 31). A failed save produces no record anywhere — the error object is explicitly cleared (`Err.Clear`, line 32).
findings.gap: Failures are unobservable. There is no trace, log line, or correlation identifier with which to reconstruct what happened during any request, agent-initiated or human.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging with a per-operation correlation ID and propagate it through the service layer from API-Q1; remove the error-swallowing handlers so failures are recorded.

compensating_controls: Log every agent invocation and its full outcome in the orchestration layer, since the target system records nothing.
Require the agent to perform a read-back verification after each write to confirm the effect.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting exists. There are no CloudWatch alarms, anomaly detectors, SLO definitions, or paging integrations in the repository (no IaC and no configuration files beyond `.gitignore`). Failure detection is manual and user-reported: the application's response to a write failure is a dialog asking the user to try again (frmCustomer.frm line 31). README.md confirms recurring failure modes — monthly .mdb corruption and common 'record locked' errors — that today are discovered by field users rather than by monitoring.
findings.gap: Error-rate and latency degradation is invisible to operators, so a failing integration surface would be detected only after users or an agent had already been failing for an extended period.
findings.recommendation: Instrument the service layer with error-rate and latency metrics and configure threshold alarms on the operations agents will consume.

compensating_controls: Alert from the agent orchestration layer on consecutive write failures or latency spikes.
Add an external synthetic check that exercises the data path on a schedule and pages on failure.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: There is no infrastructure as code: no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, Kustomize, or Ansible files exist (the repository contains exactly three tracked files — `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `frmCustomer.frm`). Infrastructure is manual by design: README.md records 'Distribution: EXE copied to each laptop by hand', 'No installer', 'File share is a single Windows file server with no failover', and 'compiled on one developer's machine'. Both `has_http_rpc_surface` and `has_auth_surface` are false, so surface-flag calibration applies and this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: No IaC definition, no change review on infrastructure, and no drift detection — but there is currently no API gateway, IAM, or network integration surface for agents, which is why this calibrates to INFO rather than RISK-QUALITY.
findings.recommendation: Define the agent-facing surface (gateway, identity, network, secrets) as code with peer-reviewed changes and drift detection at the time that surface is created in API-Q1.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: There is no CI/CD pipeline: no `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, or `buildspec.yml` exists in the repository. README.md states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine'. `has_http_rpc_surface` is false, so surface-flag calibration applies: there are no APIs to contract-test and this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: No automated build, no pipeline, and no breaking-change detection. The absence of any API surface is why this is INFO rather than RISK-QUALITY — but the absence of a build server is itself a key-person dependency.
findings.recommendation: Establish an automated build pipeline and add API contract validation to it once the API from API-Q1 exists.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: There is no deployment mechanism to roll back. Deployment is manual file copying — README.md: 'Distribution: EXE copied to each laptop by hand' and 'No installer; deployment is "copy the EXE and the .mdb template"'. There is no blue/green configuration, no canary, no feature flags, and no traffic shifting; recovery from a bad build would require locating and re-copying a prior EXE to every field laptop. `has_http_rpc_surface` is false, so surface-flag calibration applies and this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: No fast, reliable rollback path exists; recovery time is bounded by manual redistribution to every laptop. There is no deployed HTTP/RPC surface today, which is why this calibrates to INFO.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a packaged, versioned release with an automated deploy/rollback path as part of moving the agent-facing logic into the service from API-Q1.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no automated tests. The repository contains no test files, test directories, or test framework references, and README.md states outright 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine'. The write path in `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 24-34) — including its SQL construction and its error handling — has no coverage of input handling, output format, error responses, or edge cases.
findings.gap: No test coverage at all on the only data-mutating code path, so behavioural changes (including regressions in SQL construction or error handling) would reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Extract the data-access logic from the form into a testable unit and establish automated tests covering input handling and failure paths as part of introducing the build pipeline (ENG-Q2).

compensating_controls: Maintain a manual regression checklist executed against a staging copy before each hand-distributed release.
Have the agent perform read-back verification instead of trusting untested write behaviour.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: Customer data at rest is protected only by a legacy Jet database password. `frmCustomer.frm` opens `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` with `Provider=Microsoft.Jet.OLEDB.4.0` and `Jet OLEDB:Database Password=crm2005pw` (lines 7-8, 19-21). Jet database passwords are access gating, not encryption — the Access 2003 .mdb format's obfuscation is trivially recoverable and is not equivalent to encryption at rest. The file sits on an SMB share (README.md: 'Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) on a SMB file share') with no KMS key, no BitLocker/EFS configuration, and no encryption settings anywhere in the repository; the SQL Server 2012 reporting copy likewise has no documented TDE configuration.
findings.gap: The customer dataset is effectively unencrypted at rest on a file share. Anyone who can copy the .mdb file obtains the data, and the shared password offers no meaningful protection.
findings.recommendation: Migrate the data to a managed store with encryption at rest under a customer-managed key (e.g. RDS with KMS) and, in the interim, enable volume-level encryption on the file server and tighten share ACLs.

compensating_controls: Enable BitLocker/EFS on the file server volume and restrict share ACLs to the minimum principal set.
Keep the agent on a derived, de-identified dataset rather than the primary .mdb until encryption is in place.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: No API or serialization surface exists (Win32 form with ADODB data access only; no response formatting, no content-type handling) — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no operations exceeding 30s and no long-running workflows; the only operation is a single-row INSERT in cmdSave_Click.

evaluations.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
evaluations.reason: System exposes no API/HTTP surface — no endpoints, gateway, throttling, or rate-limit headers to document. Informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no priority was supplied in additionalPlanContext (not P0) and no evidence places this desktop CRM form on a shared critical path; README.md describes it as a field-sales desktop tool with nightly downstream sync.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the system exposes no list or query endpoints (frmCustomer.frm contains a single INSERT and no SELECT), so there are no unbounded result sets to constrain.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: System emits no metrics or telemetry of any kind — there is no observability surface to assess (frmCustomer.frm contains no instrumentation and the repository has no monitoring configuration). Informational signal, no finding emitted.

items.summary: Establish an agent-callable, authenticated, auditable integration surface: replace direct .mdb access with a service API, introduce machine identity and per-principal credentials, add transactional writes with idempotency, and resolve data scoping and residency. Also closes the identity, concurrency, and blast-radius safety gaps.
Harden the new surface: parameterized input validation, queryable state, schema versioning, structured logging and alerting, encryption at rest, and a staging environment.
Build out test coverage, event emission, catalog/metadata, data quality baselines, and the IaC/CI-CD governance for the agent-facing surface.

recommended_actions.action: Replace direct Access file integration with a service API over a managed datastore
recommended_actions.rationale: Direct Jet/OLEDB access to an .mdb file on an SMB share cannot be authenticated, scoped, audited, rate-limited, or versioned. Every other remediation depends on an API existing.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce machine identity and remove the shared hardcoded database credential
recommended_actions.rationale: A single compiled-in password (crm2005pw) is the whole authorization model; without per-principal identity nothing can be scoped, attributed, or revoked.

recommended_actions.action: Make writes transactional, idempotent, and auditable
recommended_actions.rationale: The only write path is a non-idempotent INSERT with On Error Resume Next against a file store that corrupts under concurrent writes — a retrying agent would duplicate and corrupt data undetectably.

recommended_actions.action: Scope and classify the customer dataset and determine residency obligations
recommended_actions.rationale: Customer personal data is reachable in full by any credential holder, is unencrypted at rest, and has no documented jurisdiction.

recommended_actions.action: Eliminate the SQL injection path and add structured input validation
recommended_actions.rationale: txtName.Text is concatenated directly into an INSERT statement; parameterizing it is a contained, high-value fix independent of the broader migration.

recommended_actions.action: Stand up a build pipeline, tests, and a staging environment
recommended_actions.rationale: The binary is compiled on one developer's machine with no tests and a production database path hardcoded as a constant — there is no safe place to validate agent behaviour.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument observability for the agent-facing path
recommended_actions.rationale: Errors are swallowed by On Error Resume Next and cleared; agent-initiated failures are currently undiagnosable.

recommended_actions.action: Add human-in-the-loop controls for agent-proposed changes
recommended_actions.rationale: Every write commits immediately with no reviewable intermediate state, so there is no application-layer defense in depth beneath the orchestrator.
